mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings and consumer spending, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 1% signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where RSAFS falls > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index above 0.5% signals stronger manufacturing output, which boosts earnings for industrial firms and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where INDPRO rises > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls above 100,000 coinciding with a rise in the unemployment rate signals a mixed labor market, which increases uncertainty and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 100,000 AND UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where PAYEMS rises > 100,000 AND UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts exceeding 10% signals a sharp contraction in residential investment, which reduces demand for construction materials and related equities, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where HOUST falls > 10% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% during a period of rising unemployment signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which reduces corporate borrowing and consumer spending, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% AND UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% AND UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% during a period of rising unemployment signals a deepening economic downturn, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 2% AND UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where RSAFS falls > 2% AND UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).
